locator: I q.3 a.3 co.: in eis non differt suppositum et natura; oportet quod Deus sit sua deitas
interpretation: The conclusion identifies God with his nature, following the distinction between material composites and self-individuating subsistent forms. Read universally over proper divine-being instances of IsGod and represent the identity within the existing Principle sort. This records the attributed conclusion as an open premise; it does not derive it from the existing generic Composite predicate or confuse Principle equality with cross-type Being equality.
